verses.20:6: And yet another war occurred in Gath, in which there was a very tall man having six digits apiece, that is, twenty-four altogether, who himself also had been born from the stock of Rapha.
verses.20:7: This man reviled Israel, and Jonathan the son of Shimea, the brother of David, struck him down. These are the sons of Rapha in Gath who fell by the hand of David and his servants.
verses.21:1: Now Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to number Israel.
verses.21:2: And David said to Joab and to the leaders of the people, "Go and number Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring me the number so that I may know."
verses.21:3: And Joab answered, "May the Lord increase His people a hundred times more than they are. Are they not all, my lord the king, your servants? Why does my lord seek this thing, which would be reckoned as a sin to Israel?"
verses.21:4: But the word of the king prevailed the more; and Joab went out and went around all Israel, and returned to Jerusalem,
verses.21:5: and gave David the number of those whom he had gone around to; and the whole number of Israel was found to be one million one hundred thousand men drawing the sword, and of Judah four hundred seventy thousand warriors.
verses.21:6: For he did not number Levi and Benjamin, because Joab was carrying out the king's command unwillingly.
verses.21:7: Now what had been commanded displeased God, and He struck Israel.
verses.21:8: And David said to God, "I have sinned greatly in doing this; I implore You, take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted foolishly."
verses.21:9: And the Lord spoke to Gad, David's seer, saying,
verses.21:10: "Go and speak to David, and say to him, 'This is what the Lord says: I give you a choice of three things; choose one, whichever you wish, and I will do it to you.'"
verses.21:11: And when Gad had come to David, he said to him, "This is what the Lord says: 'Choose what you wish:
verses.21:12: either three years of famine; or three months in which you flee your enemies and are unable to escape their sword; or three days of the sword of the Lord, and pestilence moving about in the land, and the angel of the Lord killing in all the borders of Israel.' Now therefore see what I should answer Him who sent me."
verses.21:13: And David said to Gad, "Distresses press upon me from every side; but it is better for me that I fall into the hands of the Lord, for His mercies are many, than into the hands of men."
verses.21:14: Therefore the Lord sent pestilence upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.
verses.21:15: He also sent an angel to Jerusalem to strike it; and while it was being struck, the Lord saw and took pity over the greatness of the calamity, and commanded the angel who was striking, "It is enough; now let your hand cease." Now the angel of the Lord was standing beside the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.21:16: And David, lifting up his eyes, saw the angel of the Lord standing between heaven and earth, and a drawn sword in his hand, turned against Jerusalem; and both he himself and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell prostrate to the ground.
verses.21:17: And David said to God, "Is it not I who commanded that the people be numbered? I who have sinned? I who have done evil? This flock, what has it deserved? Lord my God, let Your hand, I implore You, be turned against me and against the house of my father; but let Your people not be struck."
verses.21:18: Now the angel of the Lord commanded Gad to tell David to go up and erect an altar to the Lord God on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.21:19: Therefore David went up according to the word of Gad, which he had spoken to him in the name of the Lord.
verses.21:20: Now when Ornan looked up and saw the angel, he and his four sons with him hid themselves; for at that time he was threshing wheat on the threshing floor.
verses.21:21: Therefore as David was coming to Ornan, Ornan caught sight of him, and went out from the threshing floor to meet him, and paid homage to him, prostrate to the ground.
verses.21:22: And David said to him, "Give me the site of your threshing floor to build an altar to the Lord on it, so that you may receive as much silver as it is worth, and the plague may cease from the people."
verses.21:23: And Ornan said to David, "Take it, and let my lord the king do whatever pleases him; indeed, I also give the oxen for a burnt offering, and the threshing sledges for wood, and the wheat for a sacrifice; I will gladly provide everything."
verses.21:24: And King David said to him, "By no means will it be so, but I will give as much silver as it is worth; for I ought not to take from you and thus offer to the Lord burnt offerings without cost."
verses.21:25: Therefore David gave Ornan six hundred shekels of gold of the most exact weight for the site.
verses.21:26: And he built an altar there to the Lord, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and called upon the Lord; and He answered him with fire from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering.
verses.21:27: And the Lord commanded the angel, and he returned his sword into the sheath.
verses.21:28: Immediately therefore David, seeing that the Lord had answered him on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, sacrificed victims there.
verses.21:29: Now the tabernacle of the Lord, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offerings were at that time on the high place of Gibeon.
verses.21:30: And David could not go to the altar to implore God there, for he had been terrified with excessive fear, seeing the sword of the angel of the Lord.
verses.22:1: And David said, "This is the house of God, and this is the altar for burnt offering for Israel."
verses.22:2: And he commanded that all the proselytes from the land of Israel be gathered together, and from among them he appointed stonecutters to cut and polish stones, so that the house of God might be built.
verses.22:3: David also prepared iron in great quantity for the nails of the doors and for the joints and fastenings, and an innumerable weight of bronze.
verses.22:4: Cedar timbers also could not be estimated, which the Sidonians and the Tyrians had transported to David.
verses.22:5: And David said, "My son Solomon is a very young and delicate boy, and the house that I want to be built for the Lord must be such that it is named in all regions; therefore I will prepare what is necessary for it." And for this reason, before his death, he prepared all the supplies.
verses.22:6: And he called his son Solomon and commanded him to build a house for the Lord God of Israel.
verses.22:7: And David said to Solomon, "My son, it was my desire to build a house for the name of the Lord my God,
verses.22:8: but the word of the Lord came to me, saying, 'You have shed much blood and have waged very many wars; you will not be able to build a house for My name, since so much blood has been shed before Me.
verses.22:9: The son who will be born to you will be a most tranquil man, for I will make him rest from all his enemies all around; and for this reason he will be called Peaceful, and I will give peace and quiet in Israel all his days.
verses.22:10: He himself will build a house for My name, and he himself will be a son to Me, and I will be a father to him; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.'
verses.22:11: Now therefore, my son, may the Lord be with you, and prosper, and build a house for the Lord your God, just as He has spoken concerning you.
verses.22:12: May the Lord also grant prudence and understanding, so that you may be able to rule Israel and to keep the law of the Lord your God.
verses.22:13: For then you will be able to succeed, if you keep the commands and judgments that the Lord commanded Moses to teach Israel. Be strong and act courageously; do not fear, and do not be terrified.
verses.22:14: Look, in my poverty I have prepared the supplies for the house of the Lord: one hundred thousand talents of gold and one million talents of silver; and for bronze and iron there is no weighing, for the number is surpassed by the magnitude; I have prepared timber and stones for all the expenses.
verses.22:15: You also have very many craftsmen: stonecutters and masons, and craftsmen of wood, and men most skilled in all crafts for doing the work,
verses.22:16: in gold and silver and bronze and iron, of which there is no number. Rise therefore and do it, and the Lord will be with you."
verses.22:17: David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon,
verses.22:18: saying, "You see that the Lord your God is with you, and has given you rest all around, and has delivered all your enemies into your hands, and the land has been subdued before the Lord and before His people.
verses.22:19: Give therefore your hearts and your souls to seek the Lord your God; and rise up and build a sanctuary for the Lord God, so that the ark of the covenant of the Lord and the vessels consecrated to the Lord may be brought into the house that is being built for the name of the Lord."
verses.23:1: Therefore David, old and full of days, appointed his son Solomon king over Israel.
verses.23:2: And he assembled all the leaders of Israel, and the priests and the Levites.
verses.23:3: And the Levites were counted from thirty years of age and upward, and thirty-eight thousand men were found.
verses.23:4: From these, twenty-four thousand were chosen and assigned to the service of the house of the Lord, and of overseers and judges, six thousand.
verses.23:5: Moreover, four thousand were gatekeepers, and as many were singers, singing to the Lord with the instruments that he had made for singing.
verses.23:6: And David distributed them according to the divisions of the sons of Levi: namely, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.23:7: The sons of Gershon: Ladan and Shimei.
verses.23:8: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel, three.
verses.23:9: The sons of Shimei: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran, three; these were the chiefs of the families of Ladan.
verses.23:10: Furthermore, the sons of Shimei: Leheth, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah; these were the sons of Shimei, four.
verses.23:11: Now Leheth was the first, Ziza the second; but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, and therefore they were counted as one family and one house.
verses.23:12: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.
verses.23:13: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart to minister in the Holy of Holies, he and his sons forever, and to burn incense to the Lord according to his rite, and to bless His name for all time.
verses.23:14: The sons of Moses, the man of God, were also counted in the tribe of Levi.
verses.23:15: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
verses.23:16: The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the first.
verses.23:17: Now the sons of Eliezer were Rehabiah the first, and Eliezer had no other sons. However, the sons of Rehabiah multiplied exceedingly.
verses.23:18: The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the first.
verses.23:19: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.
verses.23:20: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the first, Isshiah the second.
verses.23:21: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
verses.23:22: Now Eleazar died and had no sons, but daughters; and the sons of Kish, their brothers, took them.
verses.23:23: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth, three.
verses.23:24: These were the sons of Levi in their clans and families, chiefs according to divisions and the number of individual heads, who did the works of the service of the house of the Lord, from twenty years of age and upward.
verses.23:25: For David said, "The Lord God of Israel has given rest to His people, and a dwelling in Jerusalem forever.
verses.23:26: Nor will it any longer be the duty of the Levites to carry the tabernacle and all its vessels for ministering."
verses.23:27: Also, according to the last commands of David, the number of the sons of Levi will be reckoned from twenty years of age and upward.
verses.23:28: And they will be under the hand of the sons of Aaron for the worship of the house of the Lord, in the forecourts, and in the chambers, and in the place of purification, and in the sanctuary, and in all the works of the service of the temple of the Lord.
verses.23:29: But the priests will be over the loaves of presentation, and for the sacrifice of fine flour, and for the unleavened wafers, and the griddle, and for roasting, and over every weight and measure.
verses.23:30: And the Levites are to stand in the morning to give thanks and sing to the Lord, and likewise in the evening,
verses.23:31: both at the offering of the burnt offerings of the Lord and on the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the other solemn feasts, according to the number and ceremonies of each thing, continually before the Lord.
verses.23:32: And let them keep the observances of the tabernacle of the covenant, and the rite of the sanctuary, and the observance of the sons of Aaron their brothers, to minister in the house of the Lord.
verses.24:1: Now these were the divisions for the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
verses.24:2: But Nadab and Abihu died before their father without children, and Eleazar and Ithamar served in the priesthood.
verses.24:3: And David divided them, that is, Zadok of the sons of Eleazar, and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, according to their divisions and service.
verses.24:4: And many more sons of Eleazar were found among the chief men than sons of Ithamar. And he divided for them, that is, for the sons of Eleazar, sixteen chiefs by families, and for the sons of Ithamar, eight by their families and houses.
verses.24:5: Moreover, he divided both families among themselves by lots; for there were leaders of the sanctuary and leaders of God both from the sons of Eleazar and from the sons of Ithamar.
verses.24:6: And Shemaiah the son of Nethanel, the scribe, a Levite, recorded them before the king and the leaders, and Zadok the priest, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and also the chiefs of the priestly and Levitical families: one house, which presided over the rest, of Eleazar, and the other house, which had the rest under it, of Ithamar.
verses.24:7: Now the first lot came out for Jehoiarib, the second for Jedaiah,
verses.24:8: the third for Harim, the fourth for Seorim,
verses.24:9: the fifth for Malchijah, the sixth for Mijamin,
verses.24:10: the seventh for Hakkoz, the eighth for Abijah,
verses.24:11: the ninth for Jeshua, the tenth for Shecaniah,
verses.24:12: the eleventh for Eliashib, the twelfth for Jakim,
verses.24:13: the thirteenth for Huppah, the fourteenth for Jeshebeab,
verses.24:14: the fifteenth for Bilgah, the sixteenth for Immer,
verses.24:15: the seventeenth for Hezir, the eighteenth for Happizzez,
verses.24:16: the nineteenth for Pethahiah, the twentieth for Jehezkel,
verses.24:17: the twenty-first for Jachin, the twenty-second for Gamul,
verses.24:18: the twenty-third for Delaiah, the twenty-fourth for Maaziah.
verses.24:19: These were their divisions according to their services, to enter the house of the Lord, and according to their rite under the hand of Aaron their father, just as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
verses.24:20: Now of the sons of Levi who remained: from the sons of Amram was Shubael, and from the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
verses.24:21: Also from the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
verses.24:22: And the son of Izhar was Shelomoth, and the son of Shelomoth was Jahath;
verses.24:23: and his son: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.
verses.24:24: The son of Uzziel was Micah; the son of Micah, Shamir.
verses.24:25: The brother of Micah was Isshiah; and the son of Isshiah, Zechariah.
verses.24:26: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The son of Jaaziah: Beno.
verses.24:27: Also the son of Merari: Jaaziah, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
verses.24:28: Moreover, the son of Mahli was Eleazar, who had no children.
verses.24:29: And the son of Kish was Jerahmeel.
verses.24:30: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth; these were the sons of Levi according to the houses of their families.
verses.24:31: And they also cast lots opposite their brothers, the sons of Aaron, before King David, and Zadok, and Ahimelech, and the chiefs of the priestly and Levitical families, both the greater and the lesser; the lot divided all equally.
verses.25:1: Therefore David and the officers of the army set apart for service the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, who were to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals according to their number, serving in the office assigned to them.
verses.25:2: Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, the sons of Asaph, under the hand of Asaph, who prophesied beside the king.
verses.25:3: As for Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the hand of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with a lyre over those giving thanks to and praising the Lord.
verses.25:4: As for Heman also, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
verses.25:5: All these were the sons of Heman, the king's seer in the words of God, to exalt the horn; and God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
verses.25:6: All of them were distributed under the hand of their father for singing in the temple of the Lord, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the services of the house of the Lord beside the king: namely, Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman.
verses.25:7: Now their number, together with their brothers who taught the song of the Lord, all of them teachers, was two hundred eighty-eight.
verses.25:8: And they cast lots by their turns, equally, the greater as well as the lesser, the learned and the unlearned alike.
verses.25:9: And the first lot came out for Joseph, who was of Asaph. The second for Gedaliah, for him and his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:10: The third for Zaccur, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:11: The fourth for Izri, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:12: The fifth for Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:13: The sixth for Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:14: The seventh for Jesharelah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:15: The eighth for Jeshaiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:16: The ninth for Mattaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:17: The tenth for Shemaiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:18: The eleventh for Azarel, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:19: The twelfth for Hashabiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:20: The thirteenth for Shubael, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:21: The fourteenth for Mattithiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:22: The fifteenth for Jerimoth, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:23: The sixteenth for Hananiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:24: The seventeenth for Joshbekashah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:25: The eighteenth for Hanani, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:26: The nineteenth for Mallothi, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:27: The twentieth for Eliathah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:28: The twenty-first for Hothir, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:29: The twenty-second for Giddalti, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:30: The twenty-third for Mahazioth, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.25:31: The twenty-fourth for Romamti-ezer, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.26:1: Now the divisions of the gatekeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah, the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.
verses.26:2: The sons of Meshelemiah: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
verses.26:3: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Elioenai the seventh.
verses.26:4: And the sons of Obed-edom: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
verses.26:5: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth; because the Lord blessed him.
verses.26:6: Also to his son Shemaiah sons were born, rulers of their families, for they were very strong men.
verses.26:7: Therefore the sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad; his brothers, very strong men: Elihu and Semachiah also.
verses.26:8: All these were of the sons of Obed-edom: they and their sons and their brothers, very strong for service, sixty-two of Obed-edom.
verses.26:9: And the sons of Meshelemiah and their brothers, very vigorous men, were eighteen.
verses.26:10: Now of Hosah, that is, of the sons of Merari: Shimri was chief (for he had not had a firstborn, and therefore his father had appointed him as chief),
verses.26:11: Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth; all these sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.
verses.26:12: These were divided as gatekeepers, so that the chiefs of the watches, just as their brothers also, might always serve in the house of the Lord.
verses.26:13: Therefore lots were cast equally, for both the small and the great, according to their families, for each of the gates.
verses.26:14: So the eastern lot fell to Shelemiah. And to his son Zechariah, a very prudent and learned man, the northern quarter fell by lot.
verses.26:15: And to Obed-edom and his sons, to the south, in which part of the house was the council of the elders.
verses.26:16: To Shuppim and Hosah, to the west, beside the gate that leads to the road of ascent, watch opposite watch.
verses.26:17: To the east were six Levites; to the north, four each day; to the south likewise, four a day; and where the council was, two and two.
verses.26:18: Also in the chambers of the gatekeepers to the west, four on the road, and two at the chambers.
verses.26:19: These are the divisions of the gatekeepers of the sons of Korah and Merari.
verses.26:20: Now Ahijah was over the treasuries of the house of God and the vessels of the holy things.
verses.26:21: The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonite: of Ladan, the chiefs of the families of Ladan and of the Gershonite: Jehieli.
verses.26:22: The sons of Jehieli: Zetham and Joel his brothers, over the treasuries of the house of the Lord.
verses.26:23: For the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites.
verses.26:24: Now Shubael, the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was set over the treasuries.
verses.26:25: Also his brothers: Eliezer, whose son was Rehabiah, and his son Jeshaiah, and his son Joram, and his son also Zichri, and his son Shelomith.
verses.26:26: This Shelomith and his brothers were over the treasuries of the holy things that King David, the chiefs of the families, the tribunes, the centurions, and the commanders of the army sanctified,
verses.26:27: from the wars and the spoils of the battles, which they had consecrated for the restoration and furnishing of the temple of the Lord.
verses.26:28: And all these things Samuel the seer, Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah sanctified: all who had sanctified them by the hand of Shelomith and his brothers.
verses.26:29: Now over the Izharites were Chenaniah and his sons, for the outside works over Israel, to teach and to judge them.
verses.26:30: And of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, very strong men, one thousand seven hundred, were over Israel beyond the Jordan toward the west, in all the works of the Lord and for the service of the king.
verses.26:31: Now Jeriah was chief of the Hebronites according to their families and clans. In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were numbered, and very strong men were found in Jazer of Gilead,
verses.26:32: and his brothers of vigorous age, two thousand seven hundred chiefs of families. And King David set them over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, for every service of God and of the king.
verses.27:1: Now the sons of Israel according to their number, the leaders of families, tribunes, and centurions, and officers, who served the king according to their contingents, coming in and going out month by month in the year, were each in charge of twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:2: Over the first contingent in the first month, Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel was in charge, and under him were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:3: He was from the sons of Perez, the leader of all the leaders in the army in the first month.
verses.27:4: Dodai the Ahohite had the contingent of the second month, and after him another named Mikloth, who commanded a part of the army of twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:5: Also, the commander of the third contingent in the third month was Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, the priest; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:6: This is Benaiah, the mightiest among the thirty and over the thirty; and his son Ammizabad was in charge of his contingent.
verses.27:7: The fourth, in the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; and in his contingent were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:8: The fifth, in the fifth month, was the leader Shamhuth the Izrahite; and in his contingent were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:9: The sixth, in the sixth month, was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; and in his contingent were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:10: The seventh, in the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, from the sons of Ephraim; and in his contingent were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:11: The eighth, in the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, from the lineage of Zerah; and in his contingent were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:12: The ninth, in the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, from the sons of Jemini; and in his contingent were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:13: The tenth, in the tenth month, was Maharai, himself also a Netophathite, from the lineage of Zerah; and in his contingent were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:14: The eleventh, in the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, from the sons of Ephraim; and in his contingent were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:15: The twelfth, in the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, from the lineage of Othniel; and in his contingent were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:16: Furthermore, those in charge of the tribes of Israel were: over the Reubenites, the chief Eliezer the son of Zichri; over the Simeonites, the chief Shephatiah the son of Maacah;
verses.27:17: over the Levites, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; over the Aaronites, Zadok;
verses.27:18: over Judah, Elihu the brother of David; over Issachar, Omri the son of Michael;
verses.27:19: over the Zebulunites, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; over the Naphtalites, Jerimoth the son of Azriel;
verses.27:20: over the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; over the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah;
verses.27:21: and over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; and over Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner;
verses.27:22: and over Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These were the leaders of the sons of Israel.
verses.27:23: But David was unwilling to count those from twenty years old and under, because the Lord had said that He would multiply Israel like the stars of heaven.
verses.27:24: Joab the son of Zeruiah had begun to count, and did not finish, because over this wrath had burst upon Israel; and therefore the number of those who had been registered was not entered into the annals of King David.
verses.27:25: Now over the treasuries of the king was Azmaveth the son of Adiel; and over those treasuries that were in the cities, and in the villages, and in the towers, Jonathan the son of Uzziah presided.
verses.27:26: And over the farm work and the farmers who tilled the land, Ezri the son of Chelub was in charge;
verses.27:27: and over the cultivators of the vineyards, Shemaiah the Ramathite; and over the wine cellars, Zabdi the Aphonite.
verses.27:28: Moreover, over the olive groves and fig groves that were in the plains was Baal-hanan the Gederite; and over the storehouses of oil was Joash.
verses.27:29: Furthermore, over the herds that grazed in Sharon, Shitrai the Sharonite was appointed; and over the cattle in the valleys, Shaphat the son of Adlai;
verses.27:30: and over the camels, Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the donkeys, Jehdeiah the Meronothite;
verses.27:31: and over the sheep also, Jaziz the Hagrite. All these were the officials of King David's property.
verses.27:32: Now Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor, a prudent and learned man; he and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni were with the king's sons.
verses.27:33: Ahithophel was also a counselor of the king, and Hushai the Archite was the king's friend.
verses.27:34: After Ahithophel were Jehoiada the son of Benaiah and Abiathar. And the commander of the king's army was Joab.
verses.28:1: David therefore summoned all the leaders of Israel, the chiefs of the tribes, and the overseers of the contingents who served the king, also the tribunes and centurions, and those who were in charge of the property and possessions of the king, and his sons with the eunuchs, and the mighty men and all the strongest in the army of Jerusalem.
verses.28:2: And when the king had risen and stood up, he said, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people: I planned to build a house in which the ark of the covenant of the Lord and the footstool of the feet of our God might rest, and I prepared everything for building.
verses.28:3: But God said to me, 'You will not build a house for My name, since you are a fighting man and have shed blood.'
verses.28:4: Yet the Lord God of Israel chose me from the entire house of my father to be king over Israel forever; for from Judah He chose the leaders, and from the house of Judah, the house of my father, and among the sons of my father it pleased Him to choose me as king over all Israel.
verses.28:5: And also from my sons (for the Lord has given me many sons) He chose my son Solomon to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel,
verses.28:6: and He said to me, 'Your son Solomon will build My house and My courts; for I have chosen him for Myself as a son, and I will be a father to him.
verses.28:7: And I will establish his kingdom forever, if he perseveres in doing My precepts and judgments, just as today.'
verses.28:8: Now therefore, before the entire assembly of Israel, with our God listening, keep and seek out all the commandments of the Lord our God, so that you may possess the good land and leave it to your sons after you forever.
verses.28:9: And you, my son Solomon, know the God of your father and serve Him with a perfect heart and a willing spirit; for the Lord examines all hearts and understands all the thoughts of minds. If you seek Him, you will find Him; but if you abandon Him, He will cast you away forever.
verses.28:10: Now therefore, since the Lord has chosen you to build the house of the sanctuary, be strong and accomplish it."
verses.28:11: Then David gave to his son Solomon the plan of the portico, and of the temple, and of the storerooms, and of the upper room, and of the chambers in the inner recesses, and of the house of propitiation,
verses.28:12: and also of all that he had planned, of the courts and of the side chambers all around, for the treasuries of the house of the Lord and for the treasuries of the holy things,
verses.28:13: and of the priestly and Levitical divisions, for all the works of the house of the Lord and for all the vessels of the service of the temple of the Lord.
verses.28:14: Gold by weight for each vessel of service. Also the weight of silver according to the variety of the vessels and works.
verses.28:15: And also for the golden lampstands and for their lamps, gold according to the measure of each lampstand and the lamps. Likewise also for the silver lampstands and for their lamps, he delivered the weight of silver according to the difference in measure.
verses.28:16: He also gave gold for the tables of presentation according to the variety of the tables; likewise also silver for the other silver tables.
verses.28:17: Also for the forks, and the bowls, and the censers of purest gold, and for the little golden lions, he apportioned the weight according to the kind of measure for each little lion. Likewise also for the silver lions he set aside a different weight of silver.
verses.28:18: And for the altar on which incense is burned, he gave purest gold, so that from it might be made the likeness of the chariot of the cherubim stretching out their wings and veiling the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
verses.28:19: "All things," he said, "came to me written by the hand of the Lord, so that I might understand all the works of the pattern."
verses.28:20: David also said to his son Solomon, "Act courageously, and be strong, and do it; do not fear and do not be terrified, for the Lord my God will be with you, and He will not leave you nor abandon you until you accomplish all the work of the service of the house of the Lord.
verses.28:21: Here are the divisions of the priests and Levites: for every service of the house of the Lord they stand by you and are ready, and both the leaders and the people know how to carry out all your commands."
verses.29:1: And King David spoke to the whole assembly: "God has chosen my son Solomon alone, still a boy and very tender; for the work is great, and indeed a dwelling is not being prepared for man, but for God.
verses.29:2: Now with all my strength I have prepared the supplies for the house of my God: gold for gold vessels, and silver for silver ones, bronze for bronze ones, iron for iron ones, wood for wooden ones, and onyx stones, and stones like antimony and of various colors, and every precious stone, and Parian marble in greatest abundance;
verses.29:3: and in addition to these things which I have offered for the house of my God, from my own private wealth I give gold and silver for the temple of my God, apart from those things which I have prepared for the holy sanctuary:
verses.29:4: three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of most refined silver for gilding the walls of the temple.
verses.29:5: And wherever gold is needed, from the gold, and wherever silver is needed, from the silver, let the works be done by the hands of craftsmen; and if anyone offers willingly, let him fill his hand today and offer what he wishes to the Lord."
verses.29:6: Therefore the leaders of the families and the nobles of the tribes of Israel, the tribunes also and the centurions, and the leaders of the king's possessions made pledges.
verses.29:7: And they gave for the works of the house of God five thousand talents of gold and ten thousand solidi; ten thousand talents of silver and eighteen thousand talents of bronze; and also one hundred thousand talents of iron.
verses.29:8: And anyone with whom stones were found gave them into the treasuries of the house of the Lord by the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
verses.29:9: And the people rejoiced when they willingly promised their vows, because with a whole heart they were offering them to the Lord; and King David also rejoiced with great joy.
verses.29:10: And he blessed the Lord before the entire multitude, and said: "Blessed are You, Lord God of Israel our father, from eternity to eternity.
verses.29:11: Yours, Lord, are magnificence, and power, and glory, and victory, and to You belongs praise; for all things that are in heaven and on earth are Yours; Yours, Lord, is the kingdom, and You are above all rulers.
verses.29:12: Yours are riches, and Yours is glory; You rule over all. In Your hand are strength and power; in Your hand are greatness and dominion over all.
verses.29:13: Now therefore, our God, we give thanks to You, and we praise Your renowned name.
verses.29:14: Who am I, and who is my people, that we should be able to promise all these things to You? All things are Yours, and what we have received from Your hand we have given to You.
verses.29:15: For we are foreigners before You, and sojourners, just like all our fathers. Our days are like a shadow on the earth, and there is no lingering.
verses.29:16: Lord our God, all this abundance which we have prepared so that a house might be built for Your holy name is from Your hand, and all things are Yours.
verses.29:17: I know, my God, that You test hearts and love sincerity; therefore I also, in the sincerity of my heart, have gladly offered all these things, and with immense joy I have seen Your people who are found here offering gifts to You.
verses.29:18: Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel our fathers, keep forever this willingness of their heart, and may this mind always remain in reverence toward You.
verses.29:19: To my son Solomon also give a perfect heart, so that he may keep Your commandments, Your testimonies, and Your ceremonies, and do everything, and build the sanctuary whose supplies I have prepared."
verses.29:20: Then David commanded the entire assembly: "Bless the Lord our God." And the whole assembly blessed the Lord God of their fathers; and they bowed themselves down, and worshiped God, and then the king.
verses.29:21: And they sacrificed victims to the Lord, and on the following day they offered burnt offerings: one thousand bulls, one thousand rams, one thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and with every rite in greatest abundance for all Israel.
verses.29:22: And they ate and drank before the Lord on that day with great gladness. And they anointed Solomon the son of David a second time. Now they anointed him to the Lord as ruler, and Zadok as high priest.
verses.29:23: And Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord as king in place of his father David, and he pleased everyone, and all Israel obeyed him.
verses.29:24: Moreover, all the leaders, and the mighty men, and all the sons of King David gave their hand and were subject to King Solomon.
verses.29:25: Therefore the Lord magnified Solomon over all Israel, and gave him a glory of kingship such as no king of Israel before him had.
verses.29:26: Thus David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
verses.29:27: And the days during which he reigned over Israel were forty years: in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem thirty-three years.
verses.29:28: And he died in a good old age, full of days, and of riches, and of glory; and his son Solomon reigned in his place.
verses.29:29: Now the acts of King David, first and last, are written in the book of Samuel the seer, and in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the scroll of Gad the seer,
verses.29:30: and those of his entire kingdom, and of his might, and of the times that passed under him, whether in Israel or in all the kingdoms of the lands.

notes.1:6: The Vulgate reads Riphath (agreeing with Gen 10:3, the Septuagint, and several Hebrew manuscripts), whereas the standard Masoretic Text of 1 Chronicles 1:6 reads Diphath.
notes.1:7: The Vulgate reads Dodanim (agreeing with Gen 10:4 and several Hebrew manuscripts), whereas the standard Masoretic Text of 1 Chronicles 1:7 reads Rodanim.
notes.1:32: The closing sentence listing the sons of Dedan (Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim) appears in the Clementine Vulgate (parallel to Gen 25:3 and some Septuagint witnesses) but is absent from the Masoretic Text of 1 Chronicles 1:32.
notes.1:50: The Vulgate reads Phau (Pau, agreeing with Gen 36:39 and the Septuagint), whereas the Masoretic Text of 1 Chronicles 1:50 reads Pai.
notes.1:51: The Vulgate explicitly states that chiefs "began to be in place of kings" (duces pro regibus ... esse coeperunt), clarifying the shift in Edomite governance where the Masoretic Text simply notes Hadad's death before listing the chiefs.
notes.2:18: Vulgate reads "took a wife named Azubah, by whom he fathered Jerioth," presenting Jerioth as a child of Caleb and Azubah rather than a second wife as in the Hebrew text.
notes.2:24: Vulgate reads "when Hezron had died, Caleb went in to Ephrathah," taking Caleb-ephrathah (a place name in the Hebrew text) as Caleb taking Ephrathah as his wife.
notes.2:25: Vulgate reads the proper name Aram, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Oren.
notes.2:49: Vulgate makes Shaaph, the father of Madmannah, the subject who fathered Sheva, whereas the Hebrew text lists both Shaaph and Sheva as sons borne by Maacah.
notes.2:52: Vulgate translates the Hebrew names Haroeh and half of the Menuhoth literally as "who saw half of the resting places" (Latin qui videbat dimidium requietionum).
notes.2:54: Vulgate renders the Hebrew names Atroth-beth-joab and half of the Manahathites, the Zorites as "the crowns of the house of Joab, and half of the resting place of the Zorites" (Latin coronae domus Joab, et dimidium requietionis Sarai).
notes.2:55: Vulgate translates the Hebrew clan names Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Sucathites etymologically as "singing and resounding, and dwelling in tents," and renders Hebrew "from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab" as "from the heat of the father of the house of Rechab" (Latin de Calore patris domus Rechab, translating Hammath as "heat" with genitive patris).
notes.3:5: Vulgate reads 'Bathsheba' (Latin Bethsabee, as in 2 Samuel 11:3), whereas the Hebrew text of 1 Chronicles 3:5 reads 'Bath-shua.'
notes.3:17: Vulgate treats Asir ('Assir') as the proper name of Jeconiah's first son; the Hebrew 'assir can also be read as an epithet of Jeconiah, 'the captive.'
notes.3:18: Vulgate reads 'Sama,' corresponding to 'Hoshama' in the Hebrew text.
notes.3:21: Vulgate presents the names after Pelatiah as a continuous father-to-son lineage, whereas the Hebrew text lists separate collateral families ('the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan...').
notes.3:23: Vulgate uses the singular 'son' (Filius) even though three names are listed and counted.
notes.4:10: Jabez's prayer preserves the unfinished conditional wish construction ('If in blessing You bless me...'); Vulgate renders the final petition literally as 'cause me not to be oppressed by evil' (a malitia non opprimi).
notes.4:11: Vulgate reads 'Caleb' (agreeing with the Septuagint), whereas the Hebrew text reads 'Chelub.'
notes.4:18: Vulgate treats the Hebrew 'his Judean wife' as a proper name, Judaia; similarly, in 4:19 it takes 'Garmi' as a son's name rather than 'the Garmite,' and in 4:20 renders 'Ben-hanan' as 'the son of Hanan.'
notes.4:22: In 4:21-23, the Vulgate translates several Hebrew proper names by etymology and tradition: 'house of the oath' (Beth-ashbea), 'he who made the sun stand still,' 'men of Falsehood,' 'Secure,' 'Burning,' and 'who returned to Lahem' (Jokim, Cozeba, Joash, Saraph, Jashubi-lehem), and 'plantations' and 'hedges' (Netaim and Gederah).
notes.4:41: Vulgate reads 'the inhabitants' (habitatores) where the Hebrew text names 'the Meunites,' and uses first-person plural ('whom we recorded above by name') rather than a passive participle.
notes.5:2: The Vulgate reads plural principes germinati sunt ("leaders sprang forth") from Judah's stock, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads singular ("a ruler came from him").
notes.5:15: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew personal name Ahi as the common noun Fratres ("brothers") and makes filii ("sons") plural, while keeping princeps ("leader") singular.
notes.5:19: The Vulgate translates Hebrew Jetur as the plural gentilic Ituraei ("Itureans") and makes the Itureans, Naphish, and Nodab the subjects of praebuerunt eis auxilium ("gave them aid") in 5:20, whereas the Hebrew lists them as opponents alongside the Hagrites and uses a passive verb ("they were helped against them").
notes.5:26: The Vulgate keeps the place name Lahela, fusing the Hebrew preposition la- ("to") with the place name Halah while also supplying the Latin preposition in ("to") before it.
notes.5:27: This text numbers these verses 5:27-41, as the Hebrew does; the printed Sixto-Clementine edition numbers them 6:1-15.
notes.6:1: This text follows the Hebrew numbering of chapter 6 (6:1-66); the printed Sixto-Clementine edition numbers these verses 6:16-81.
notes.6:13: The Vulgate reads 'primogenitus Vasseni, et Abia' ('the firstborn Vashni, and Abijah'), following the Hebrew consonantal text where 'Vashni' is taken as the firstborn's name rather than 'Joel' with 'and the second, Abijah' (compare Joel son of Samuel in v. 18 and 1 Sam 8:2).
notes.6:16: The Vulgate reads 'super cantores' ('over the singers') and 'ex quo collocata est arca' ('from the time the ark was set in place') where the Hebrew has 'over the service of song' and 'after the ark had rest'; likewise, v. 17 has 'tabernaculo testimonii' ('the tabernacle of the testimony') for Hebrew 'the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.'
notes.6:19: The Vulgate has several distinct proper names here and in vv. 29-31: 'Thohu' ('Tohu', matching 1 Sam 1:1) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'Toah'; in v. 29 'Cusi' ('Cushi', related to 'Kushaiah' in 1 Chr 15:17) for Hebrew 'Kishi'; and in v. 31 'Amasai' for Hebrew 'Amzi.'
notes.6:33: The Vulgate reads 'domus Domini' ('the house of the Lord') where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'the house of God,' and links the Levites by the relative clause 'qui ordinati sunt' ('who were assigned').
notes.6:34: The Vulgate reads 'adolebant incensum' ('burned incense') for both altars and 'ut precarentur pro Israel' ('to pray for Israel') where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'made offerings' and 'to make atonement for Israel.'
notes.6:40: Here and throughout vv. 40-66, the Vulgate renders the open lands surrounding Levitical cities as 'suburbana' ('outskirts') where the Hebrew has 'pasturelands.'
notes.6:46: The Vulgate reads 'de cognatione sua dederunt ... in possessionem' ('from their clan, they gave ... as a possession') where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'from the family of the tribe ... by lot.'
notes.6:50: The Vulgate reads 'quas vocaverunt nominibus suis' ('which they called by their names') where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'which are mentioned by name.'
notes.7:15: The Vulgate explicitly reads 'wives for his sons' (uxores filiis suis), identifying Huppim and Shuppim as sons of Machir, whereas the Hebrew reads 'a wife for Huppim and for Shuppim' without 'his sons.'
notes.7:18: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew personal names Hammolecheth ('the queen') and Ishhod ('man of splendor') directly into Latin as Regina ('Queen') and Virum decorum ('Handsome Man').
notes.7:21: The Vulgate adds 'and his son' before Ezer and Elead and renders the Hebrew 'their livestock' as 'their possessions' (possessiones eorum).
notes.7:28: 'Daughters' is a literal rendering of the biblical idiom for dependent outlying villages surrounding a main town. The Vulgate reads 'Aza' (reflecting a Hebrew variant for Azzah/Gaza), whereas the standard Masoretic Hebrew text reads 'Ayyah.'
notes.7:33: The Vulgate reads 'Chamaal' (reflecting an initial Hebrew kaf), whereas the standard Hebrew text reads 'Bimhal' (initial bet).
notes.8:7: The abrupt transition follows the Latin and Hebrew closely, with the singular pronoun "he himself" (ipse) singling out Gera as the one who carried them away and fathered Uzza and Ahihud.
notes.8:9: The Vulgate reads Mosa here, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Mesha.
notes.8:11: The Vulgate reads Mehusim as a distinct proper name and subject of "fathered," whereas the Hebrew reads me-Chushim ("by Hushim"), referring back to Shaharaim's wife Hushim in v. 8.
notes.8:29: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew phrase "the father of Gibeon" (named Jeiel in 1 Chronicles 9:35) as a personal name, Abigabaon, while preserving the plural verb habitaverunt ("lived") from the Hebrew.
notes.8:31: The Vulgate includes "and Mikloth" (et Macelloth) at the end of the verse, agreeing with the Septuagint and 1 Chronicles 9:37, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text omits Mikloth in v. 31 before introducing him in v. 32.
notes.9:1: The Vulgate joins "and Judah" to the book title ("the book of the kings of Israel and Judah") and reads "and they were carried away," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text begins the following clause with "and Judah was carried away into exile."
notes.9:15: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew personal name Heresh as the occupation "the carpenter" (carpentarius), taking it from the Hebrew noun for a craftsman.
notes.9:20: The Vulgate reads "before the Lord" (coram Domino), combining elements that the Hebrew Masoretic Text divides as "in time past; the Lord was with him."
notes.9:25: The Vulgate renders the weekly rotation as "on their sabbaths" (in sabbatis suis), whereas the Hebrew reads "every seven days."
notes.9:41: In agreement with the Septuagint and the parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 8:35, the Vulgate includes "and Ahaz" among the sons of Micah, which is absent in the Hebrew Masoretic Text of this verse.
notes.10:9: The Vulgate reads "so that it might be carried around and shown to the temples of the idols and to the peoples," whereas the Hebrew reads "to carry the good news to their idols and to the people."
notes.10:13: The Vulgate uses the explicitly feminine term pythonissam ("a female medium"), identifying the medium of Endor (1 Samuel 28), where the Hebrew term is not grammatically feminine.
notes.10:14: The Vulgate reads "and did not hope in the Lord" (nec speraverit in Domino), whereas the Hebrew reads "and did not inquire of the Lord."
notes.11:12: The Vulgate translates Hebrew ben-Dodo ("son of Dodo") literally as a common noun, "the son of his uncle" (filius patrui ejus), both here and in 11:26.
notes.11:21: The Vulgate resolves a difficult Hebrew phrase by explicitly contrasting "the second three" (tres secundos) with "the first three" (tres primos).
notes.11:22: The Vulgate leaves the obscure Hebrew term ariel untranslated (duos ariel Moab); it is variously understood as "lion-like warriors" or "sons of Ariel."
notes.11:25: Literally "at his ear" (ad auriculam suam), rendering Hebrew mishma'to ("bodyguard" or "listening council") to denote David's trusted personal counselor and guard.
notes.11:35: This Latin text lacks "Eliphal the son of Ur," present here in the Hebrew Masoretic Text; in this warrior roster it also has distinct proper-name readings including Pharonite (11:27), Thosaite (11:45), and Mahumite, Josaia, and Masobia (11:46).
notes.12:4: Here 12:4 contains what the Hebrew divides into verses 4 and 5, so there is no separate 12:5; the Latin reads Samaias (Shemaiah) where the Hebrew has Ishmaiah.
notes.12:9: The Vulgate reads 'while he was hiding in the wilderness' (cum lateret in deserto), whereas the Hebrew text reads 'to the stronghold in the wilderness.'
notes.12:20: The Vulgate reads 'yet he did not fight with them' (et non dimicavit cum eis), referring to David, where the Hebrew reads 'they did not help them.'
notes.12:21: The Clementine Vulgate lists eight leaders from Manasseh by repeating Adnah and Jozabad (Ednas, et Jozabad) twice, whereas the Hebrew text lists seven names (repeating only Jozabad).
notes.12:41: The Vulgate reads 'rams' (arietes) for the Hebrew collective 'sheep/flocks,' and specifies 'loaves ... for eating' (panes ... ad vescendum).
notes.13:1: The Vulgate uses the Roman military titles 'tribunes' (tribunis) and 'centurions' (centurionibus) to render the Hebrew commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.
notes.13:6: The Vulgate reads 'every man of Israel' (omnis vir Israel) and translates Baalah as 'the hill of Kiriath-jearim' (ad collem Cariathiarim), concluding with 'where His name was invoked' (ubi invocatum est nomen ejus).
notes.13:7: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew proper name Ahio as the common noun 'his brother' (frater ejus).
notes.13:9: The Vulgate has a singular verb ('when he had arrived,' pervenisset) and describes 'an unruly ox' that 'had tilted it a little' (bos quippe lasciviens paululum inclinaverat eam), where the Hebrew says the oxen stumbled.
notes.13:11: The Vulgate reads 'was grieved' (contristatus est) rather than 'was angry,' and renders both the verb and the place name Perez-uzza using the Latin root for 'divide' (divisisset ... Divisio Ozae).
notes.14:2: The Vulgate reads 'over His people Israel' (super populum ejus Israel), whereas the Hebrew reads 'for the sake of His people Israel.'
notes.14:5: The Vulgate spells both 14:5 and 14:7 identically as Eliphalet (Eliphelet), whereas the Hebrew distinguishes Elpelet in verse 5 from Eliphelet in verse 7.
notes.14:14: Following the Septuagint, the Vulgate renders the Hebrew baca-trees (perhaps balsam or mulberry trees) as 'pear trees' (pyrorum) here and in verse 15.
notes.15:13: Vulgate illicitum quid nobis agentibus ("by our doing something unlawful") echoes illicitum est in 15:2 and renders a Hebrew clause meaning "because we did not seek Him according to the ordinance."
notes.15:16: Vulgate in excelsis ("on high") renders the Hebrew infinitive for "raising [the voice]" as a locative expression meaning "in the heights."
notes.15:20: Vulgate arcana ("mysteries") translates the Hebrew musical direction al-alamot ("according to Alamoth") from the root meaning "to be hidden."
notes.15:21: Vulgate pro octava ("for the octave," literally "for the eighth") and the Greek loanword epinicion ("a song of victory") translate the Hebrew musical terms al-hasheminit ("on the Sheminith") and lenatseah ("to lead").
notes.15:22: Vulgate prophetiae ("prophecy," also in 15:27) renders Hebrew massa ("lifting up" or "musical delivery"), which elsewhere denotes a prophetic oracle.
notes.16:3: Vulgate partem assae carnis bubalae, et frixam oleo similam ("a portion of roasted beef, and fine flour fried in oil") translates two rare Hebrew food terms probably meaning "a portion of meat" (or "date cake") and "a raisin cake."
notes.16:27: Vulgate confessio ("thanksgiving," reflecting Septuagint exomologesis) denotes public praise and thanksgiving before God rather than admission of guilt, where the Hebrew text reads "splendor."
notes.16:29: Unlike the Hebrew text ("Give to the Lord the glory due His name; bring an offering"), the Clementine Vulgate construes dative nomini ejus ("to His name") with the following clause, nomini ejus levate sacrificium ("lift up a sacrifice to His name").
notes.16:36: Vulgate Et dicat omnis populo: Amen, et hymnum Domino ("And let all the people say, 'Amen,' and a hymn to the Lord") uses a jussive subjunctive (dicat) rather than the Hebrew past narrative ("and all the people said... and praised the Lord"), and the text here reads omnis populo where omnis populus would be expected.
notes.17:1: The Vulgate reads sub pellibus ("under skins"), referring to the animal-skin coverings of the tabernacle, where the Hebrew has "under curtains."
notes.17:5: The Vulgate renders this sentence distinctively as "changing the places of the tabernacle, and in a tent remaining with all Israel" (spanning vv. 5-6), whereas the Hebrew speaks of moving "from tent to tent and from dwelling to dwelling."
notes.17:16: The Vulgate reads ut praestares mihi talia ("that You would grant me such things"), whereas the Hebrew has "that You have brought me this far."
notes.17:17: The Vulgate renders a difficult Hebrew clause ("according to the rank of a man of high degree") as fecisti me spectabilem super omnes homines ("You have made me remarkable above all men").
notes.17:27: The Vulgate reads coepisti ("You have begun"), whereas the Hebrew verb means "You have been pleased."
notes.18:1: "Its daughters" (Latin filias ejus) is a literal biblical idiom for the smaller dependent towns and villages surrounding Gath.
notes.18:3: The Vulgate reads Adarezer (Hadarezer), preserving a textual variant with r rather than d (Hadadezer in 2 Samuel 8 and many Hebrew manuscripts), and explicitly adds "of the region" (regionis) before Hamath.
notes.18:7: The Vulgate reads pharetras aureas ("golden quivers"), whereas the Hebrew term probably means "golden shields."
notes.18:12: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew "Valley of Salt" as valle Salinarum ("Valley of Salt Pits"), and uses the Greco-Latin name Idumaea (Idumea) for Edom in vv. 11 and 13.
notes.18:16: The Vulgate reads Ahimelech (matching the Septuagint and 2 Samuel 8:17) where the Masoretic Hebrew has Abimelech, and transliterates Shavsha as Susa.
notes.19:3: The Vulgate uses three reconnaissance verbs ("explore, and investigate, and examine"), whereas the Hebrew has "search, overthrow, and spy out."
notes.19:4: The Vulgate reads decalvavit, et rasit ("made ... bald and shaved") and a natibus usque ad pedes ("from the buttocks down to the feet"), expanding on the Hebrew ("shaved them and cut off their garments in the middle at the hips").
notes.19:18: The Vulgate literally states that David killed "seven thousand chariots" (septem millia curruum), a metonymy for chariot crews or charioteers.
notes.19:19: The Vulgate reads transfugerunt ad David ("defected to David"), whereas the Hebrew has "made peace with David."
notes.20:2: The Vulgate reads the proper name Melchom (Milcom, the Ammonite deity) where the Hebrew consonants can also be vocalized as "their king," and adds "and from it he made a diadem for himself" where the Hebrew states that it was placed on David's head.
notes.20:3: The Vulgate adds "so that they were cut in pieces and crushed" (ita ut dissecarentur et contererentur).
notes.20:5: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew names Elhanan ("God has been gracious") and Jair (read as "forest") into Latin as Adeodatus and Saltus, and omits the name Lahmi, identifying the slain Philistine simply as "the brother of Goliath the Gittite."
notes.20:7: In the Clementine Vulgate, chapter 20 contains seven verses; the final sentence of verse 7 corresponds to verse 8 in the Hebrew text.
notes.21:15: The Vulgate reads "took pity" (misertus est) where the Hebrew verb denotes relenting or grieving.
notes.21:20: The Vulgate reads "looked up" (suspexisset), aligning with the angel standing between heaven and earth in verse 16, whereas the Hebrew text reads "turned back."
notes.21:28: The Vulgate reads "Immediately" (Protinus) where the Hebrew text reads "At that time."
notes.21:30: The Vulgate specifies "to the altar" (ad altare) where the Hebrew text reads "before it."
notes.22:2: Following the Septuagint, the Vulgate renders Hebrew gerim ("resident aliens" or "sojourners") as proselyti ("proselytes").
notes.22:9: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew name Solomon (Shelomoh) into Latin as Pacificus ("Peaceful"), preserving its wordplay with "peace" (pacem) in the next clause.
notes.22:14: The Vulgate reads "in my poverty" (in paupertate mea) where the Hebrew text means "in my affliction" or "with great pains," and concludes with "for all the expenses" rather than "and you may add to them."
notes.22:18: The Vulgate renders the opening clause as a declarative statement ("You see") rather than a rhetorical question, and reads "all your enemies into your hands" where the Hebrew has "the inhabitants of the land into my hand."
notes.23:5: The Vulgate renders verses 4-5 as third-person narration ("that he had made for singing"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text presents them as direct speech of David ("which I made for praising").
notes.23:10: The Clementine Vulgate reads Leheth (here and in v. 11), corresponding to Hebrew Jahath (cf. 24:22), and Ziza in both verses 10 and 11, where the Hebrew reads Zina in v. 10.
notes.23:13: Vulgate-distinct readings: "to minister in the Holy of Holies" (Hebrew: "to consecrate the most holy things"), "according to his rite" (Hebrew: "to minister to Him"), and "to bless His name" (dative nomini ejus; Hebrew: "to bless in His name").
notes.23:25: In the Vulgate, habitationem ("a dwelling") is a second direct object of dedit ("has given"), whereas the Hebrew reads "and He dwells in Jerusalem forever."
notes.23:29: The Vulgate explicitly introduces "But the priests" (Sacerdotes autem), assigning the duties of this verse to the priests before turning to the Levites in v. 30; the Hebrew omits "the priests" here and continues the Levitical duties.
notes.24:3: The Vulgate renders the clause with id est ("that is"), placing Zadok and Ahimelech in apposition to the priests being divided, whereas the Hebrew reads "with Zadok ... and Ahimelech" as David's assistants.
notes.24:6: Vulgate-distinct rendering of the closing clause ("one house, which presided over the rest, of Eleazar, and the other house, which had the rest under it, of Ithamar"), where the Hebrew describes drawing one father's house for Eleazar and one for Ithamar.
notes.24:23: The Vulgate reads filiusque ejus ("and his son"), linking these four men to Jahath (v. 22) and supplying "the first" (primus), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew omits the father's name here (cf. 23:19, where they are listed as sons of Hebron).
notes.24:27: The Vulgate uses singular Filius ("son"), spells Jaaziah as Oziau (here and in v. 26), and lists him directly among the sons of Merari without repeating Beno, whereas the Hebrew reads "the sons of Merari by Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri."
notes.24:31: The Vulgate summarizes the closing clause as "both the greater and the lesser; the lot divided all equally," whereas the Hebrew reads "the head of the father's house just like his younger brother."
notes.25:2: Latin 'juxta regem' literally means 'beside' or 'next to the king' (likewise in 25:6), rendering the Hebrew idiom for 'under the direction of the king.'
notes.25:3: Although the text counts six sons of Jeduthun, only five are named here (the sixth is presumably Shemaiah, Latin Semeias, who receives the tenth lot in 25:17, where the Hebrew has Shimei). The Vulgate also renders the final phrase with plural participles ('super confitentes et laudantes', 'over those giving thanks to and praising'), whereas the Hebrew has infinitives ('in giving thanks and praising').
notes.25:7: Distinctively Vulgate: Latin 'qui erudiebant ... cuncti doctores' reads actively ('who taught ... all of them teachers'), whereas the Hebrew describes them passively as 'trained' and 'skillful.'
notes.25:8: Latin 'doctus pariter et indoctus' ('the learned and the unlearned alike') renders the Hebrew contrast between 'teacher' and 'pupil.'
notes.26:10: Distinctively Vulgate: Latin 'non enim habuerat primogenitum' reads 'for he had not had a firstborn' (referring to Hosah), whereas the Hebrew states of Shimri that 'he was not the firstborn.'
notes.26:15: Distinctively Vulgate: Latin 'seniorum concilium' ('the council of the elders'; likewise 'concilium' in 26:17) interprets the Hebrew 'beit ha-asuppim' (usually understood as a storehouse) as a meeting place for the elders.
notes.26:16: The Vulgate omits the Hebrew proper name of the gate (Shallecheth), rendering the clause simply as 'beside the gate that leads to the road of ascent.' Similarly, in 26:18, Latin 'cellulis janitorum' ('chambers of the gatekeepers') translates the obscure Hebrew architectural term 'Parbar.'
notes.26:20: The Vulgate retains the personal name Ahijah ('Achias', agreeing with the Hebrew against the Septuagint's 'their brothers') and distinctively reads 'vasa sanctorum' ('vessels of the holy things') where the Hebrew has 'treasuries of the dedicated things.'
notes.26:29: Distinctively Vulgate: Latin 'Isaaritis ... praeerat' places Chenaniah and his sons 'over the Izharites' (rather than merely 'of the Izharites'), and 'ad docendum et judicandum eos' ('to teach and to judge them') translates the Hebrew nouns 'as officers and judges.'
notes.27:4: The Vulgate distinctively describes Mikloth as "after him another named Mikloth, who commanded a part of the army of twenty-four thousand" (Latin et post se alter nomine Macelloth, qui regebat partem exercitus viginti quatuor millium), whereas the Hebrew reads "of his division Mikloth was the chief officer."
notes.27:5: Latin sacerdos ("the priest") is nominative, modifying Benaiah rather than his father Jehoiada, and the Vulgate does not include the Hebrew title "chief" (rosh).
notes.27:12: Latin de filiis Jemini ("from the sons of Jemini") reflects a literal division of Hebrew Ben-yemini ("Benjaminites") into "sons of Jemini."
notes.27:27: The Vulgate reads Aphonites ("the Aphonite"), a distinct gentilic where the Hebrew has "the Shiphmite" (ha-Shifmi).
notes.27:28: Latin ficeta means "fig groves," whereas the Hebrew specifies "sycamore trees."
notes.28:1: Unlike the Hebrew, which places "to Jerusalem" at the beginning of the verse and links the king's sons to the royal estates, the Vulgate makes "his sons with the eunuchs" direct objects of David's summons and places "in the army of Jerusalem" at the end.
notes.28:9: Where the Hebrew has "every intent of the thoughts" and passive "He will be found by you," the Vulgate reads "all the thoughts of minds" (universas mentium cogitationes) and active "you will find Him" (invenies).
notes.28:12: The Vulgate reads simply "all that he had planned" (omnium quae cogitaverat), omitting the Hebrew phrase "by the Spirit."
notes.28:17: The Vulgate renders Hebrew keforim ("bowls") as kefirim ("young lions"), yielding "little golden lions" (leunculos aureos) and "silver lions" (leones argenteos), and translates Hebrew qasoth ("pitchers") as "censers" (thuribula).
notes.28:21: The Vulgate reads "house of the Lord" (Hebrew "house of God") and condenses the closing clauses to "they stand by you and are ready, and both the leaders and the people know how to carry out all your commands."
notes.29:2: Latin "quasi stibinos" ("like antimony," i.e., dark gleaming stones resembling stibnite/kohl) and "marmor Parium" ("Parian marble," famed white marble from Paros) are distinctive Vulgate renderings of the Hebrew descriptions of decorative stones and marble.
notes.29:7: Latin "solidos" translates the Hebrew darics using the Roman gold coin (solidus), matching the Vulgate's use of Roman military titles ("tribunes" and "centurions") in 29:6.
notes.29:15: Latin "et nulla est mora" ("and there is no lingering" or "no delay") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Hebrew has "and there is no hope" (or "abiding").
notes.29:20: The Vulgate reads "Deo nostro" ("our God") where the Hebrew has "your God," and adds "deinde" ("then") before "the king."
notes.29:23: Latin "et cunctis placuit" ("and he pleased everyone") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Hebrew reads "and he prospered."

unplaced.text: And Mizraim fathered Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,
as well as Pathrusim and Casluhim, from whom came the Philistines and the Caphtorim.
unplaced.note: The Clementine Vulgate treats both the Philistines and the Caphtorim as coming from Pathrusim and Casluhim.

unplaced.text: And Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, along with the Hittites,
unplaced.note: The Clementine Vulgate reads the gentilic "Hethaeum" (the Hittites) rather than the personal name Heth.

unplaced.text: the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.
And Arpachshad fathered Shelah, who himself fathered Eber.
Now two sons were born to Eber: the name of one was Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided; and the name of his brother was Joktan.
And Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
as well as Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab; all of these were the sons of Joktan.
Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all peoples.
